text: The 'computable' numbers may be described briefly as the real numbers whose expressions as a decimal are calculable by finite means. It is possible to invent a single machine which can be used to compute any computable sequence.

An automatic computing system is a device with which certain instructions can be given, and which will then carry out these instructions automatically. The device requires a central arithmetic part, a central control part, a memory that stores both instructions and numerical data, and input and output organs.

The IEEE Standard for Floating-Point Arithmetic (IEEE 754) is a technical standard for floating-point computation which defines arithmetic formats, interchange formats, rounding rules, operations, and exception handling including binary32 and binary64.

UTF-8 encodes UCS characters as a varying number of octets, where the number of octets, and the value of each, depend on the integer value assigned to the character in ISO/IEC 10646. US-ASCII values do not appear otherwise in a UTF-8 encoded character stream.

CS2023 organizes computer science knowledge into core areas including Algorithms and Complexity, Architecture and Organization, Discrete Structures, Foundations of Programming Languages, Operating Systems, Parallel and Distributed Computing, Software Development Fundamentals, Software Engineering, and Security.

An introduction to mathematical modeling of computational problems, as well as common algorithms, algorithmic paradigms, and data structures used to solve these problems, emphasizing the relationship between algorithms and programming and basic performance measures and analysis techniques.

Ownership is Rust's most unique feature and has deep implications for the rest of the language. It enables Rust to make memory safety guarantees without needing a garbage collector: each value in Rust has an owner, there can only be one owner at a time, and when the owner goes out of scope, the value will be dropped.

At any given time, you can have either one mutable reference or any number of immutable references, and references must always be valid. Unsafe Rust unlocks five actions: dereferencing raw pointers, calling unsafe functions, accessing mutable statics, implementing unsafe traits, and accessing union fields.

Safe Rust is a sound language: no matter what, Safe Rust cannot cause Undefined Behavior. Unsafe Rust is the exact same language with the same semantics, except that the programmer assumes responsibility for upholding the compiler's aliasing, alignment, initialization, and lifetime invariants.

Objects in C have storage duration (automatic, static, thread, or allocated), scope, linkage, and effective type. Dereferencing an invalid, null, or misaligned pointer, signed integer overflow, or violating strict aliasing rules results in undefined behavior.

Resource Acquisition Is Initialization (RAII) binds the life cycle of a resource that must be acquired before use to the lifetime of an object. C++20 introduces Concepts for constraining templates, Ranges for composable algorithms, Coroutines, and Modules.

Objects are Python's abstraction for data. All data in a Python program is represented by objects or by relations between objects. Every object has an identity, a type, and a value. Special method names (__init__, __iter__, __enter__, __exit__, __get__) define the Python data model protocols.

An ECMAScript agent consists of execution contexts, an execution context stack, a running execution context, a set of job queues (macrotask and microtask queues), and a heap of objects linked through prototype chains and lexical environments.

One of TypeScript's core principles is that type checking focuses on the shape that values have, sometimes called duck typing or structural subtyping. TypeScript's type system is erased completely at compile time and introduces zero runtime overhead.

C# is a modern, object-oriented, and type-safe programming language running on the Common Language Runtime (CLR), unifying value types (structs, Span<T>) and reference types (classes, records), generics without type erasure, LINQ, and task-based asynchronous programming.

The Java Virtual Machine executes class files using class loaders, a bytecode verifier, an interpreter, a Just-In-Time compiler, and automatic garbage collection under the Java Memory Model (JMM) happens-before relation, complemented in Java 21 by lightweight Virtual Threads.

Go is a general-purpose systems language designed with structural interfaces, explicit error values, garbage collection, and CSP-inspired concurrency via lightweight goroutines multiplexed onto OS threads and typed communication channels.

Kotlin enforces null safety in its type system by distinguishing nullable and non-null references at compile time, and provides structured concurrency through suspend functions, CoroutineScope, Dispatchers, and cold asynchronous Flows.

Swift combines protocol-oriented programming, copy-on-write value types, deterministic memory management via Automatic Reference Counting (ARC), and compile-time data-race safety using Sendable types and actor isolation.

The relational model represents all data as mathematical n-ary relations manipulated through relational algebra and declarative SQL queries. PostgreSQL implements Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC), Write-Ahead Logging (WAL), and cost-based query optimization.

SQLite is a self-contained, serverless, zero-configuration, transactional SQL database engine in the public domain that implements B-tree storage, ACID transactions via rollback journals or Write-Ahead Logging, CTEs, and window functions.

The shell is a command language interpreter that executes commands read from standard input or a file, performing parameter expansion, command substitution, arithmetic expansion, word splitting, pathname expansion, and redirection across pipelines.

HTML defines the semantic structure and Document Object Model (DOM) of web documents, while CSS defines the cascade, specificity, inheritance, box model, Flexbox, Grid, and responsive container queries for visual and accessible presentation.

JSON is a lightweight, text-based, language-independent data interchange format defining six structural tokens, strings, numbers, booleans, null, objects, and arrays encoded in UTF-8. YAML 1.2 is a strict superset of JSON adding anchors, aliases, and multi-document streams.

Software engineering encompasses systematic, disciplined, quantifiable approaches to software requirements, domain modeling, software architecture, clean and hexagonal design, automated verification and testing, CI/CD, observability, security by design, and long-term maintenance.

text: C was initially developed as a successor to the B programming language at Bell Labs by Ritchie between 1972 and 1973.
The C language standard precisely specifies the observable behavior of C language programs, except for the ones in the following categories:
1969: B created, based on BCPL, to replace PDP-7 assembler as the system programming language for Unix
1973: Unix re-written in C
In 1983 the American National Standards Institute (ANSI) formed a committee, X3J11, to establish a standard specification of C.
In 1989, the C standard was ratified as ANSI X3.159-1989 "Programming Language C".
This standard was ratified as an ISO standard (ISO/IEC 9899:1990) later in 1990.

new features: bool, long long, <stdint.h>, <inttypes.h>, restrict, compound literals, variable length arrays, flexible array members, designated initializers, <fenv.h>, variadic macros, complex numbers, __func__
thread-aware memory model, <stdatomic.h>, <threads.h>, type-generic functions, alignas/alignof, noreturn, static_assert,
the corrections are also applied with -std=c11, and the only difference between the options is the value of __STDC_VERSION__.
A fifth version of the C standard, known as C23, was published in 2024 as ISO/IEC 9899:2024.

For example, -std=c90 turns off certain features of GCC that are incompatible with ISO C90, such as the asm and typeof keywords, but not other GNU extensions that do not have a meaning in ISO C90, such as omitting the middle term of a ?: expression.
Use of the -std options listed above disables these extensions where they conflict with the C standard version selected.

To select this standard in GCC, use one of the options -ansi, -std=c90 or -std=iso9899:1990; to obtain all the diagnostics required by the standard, you should also specify -pedantic (or -pedantic-errors if you want them to be errors rather than warnings).
The C source file is processed by the compiler as if the following phases take place, in this exact order.
Each file introduced with the #include directive goes through phases 1 through 4, recursively.
Compilation can involve up to four stages: preprocessing, compilation proper, assembly and linking, always in that order.

Linking takes place: Translation units and library components needed to satisfy external references are collected into a program image which contains information needed for execution in its execution environment (the OS).
Object-like macros Object-like macros replace every occurrence of a defined identifier with replacement-list.
This behavior is controlled by #if, #else, #elif, #ifdef, #ifndef, #elifdef, #elifndef(since C23), and #endif directives.
When a file is included, it is processed by translation phases 1-4, which may include, recursively, expansion of the nested #include directives, up to an implementation-defined nesting limit.
undefined behavior - there are no restrictions on the behavior of the program.

Examples of undefined behavior are memory accesses outside of array bounds, signed integer overflow, null pointer dereference, modification of the same scalar more than once in an expression without sequence points, access to an object through a pointer of a different type, etc.
implementation-defined behavior - unspecified behavior where each implementation documents how the choice is made.
Undefined behavior is the name of a list of conditions that the program must not meet.
Compilers are not required to diagnose undefined behavior (although many simple situations are diagnosed), and the compiled program is not required to do anything meaningful.
Because correct C programs are free of undefined behavior, compilers may produce unexpected results when a program that actually has UB is compiled with optimization enabled:
By definition, the runtime can assume that undefined behavior never happens; therefore, some invalid conditions do not need to be checked against.

Another alternative is the LLP64 model, which maintains compatibility with 32-bit code by leaving both int and long as 32-bit.

An object in C is a region of data storage in the execution environment, the contents of which can represent values (a value is the meaning of the contents of an object, when interpreted as having a specific type).
In computer science, a pointer is an object in many programming languages that stores a memory address.
A pointer references a location in memory, and obtaining the value stored at that location is known as dereferencing the pointer.

A pointer whose value is null does not point to an object or a function (dereferencing a null pointer is undefined behavior), and compares equal to all pointers of the same type whose value is also null.

In general, a function that receives a pointer argument almost always needs to check if the value is null and handle that case differently (for example, free does nothing when a null pointer is passed).
(since C99) lvalue expressions of array type, when used in most contexts, undergo an implicit conversion to the pointer to the first element of the array.

Because of the array-to-pointer implicit conversion, pointer to the first element of an array can be initialized with an expression of array type: Certain addition, subtraction, compound assignment, increment, and decrement operators are defined for pointers to elements of arrays.
In languages that allow pointer arithmetic, arithmetic on pointers takes into account the size of the type.
For the purpose of pointer arithmetic, a pointer to an object that is not an element of any array is treated as a pointer to the first element of an array of size 1.
Objects are created by declarations, allocation functions, string literals, compound literals, and by non-lvalue expressions that return structures or unions with array members.

For the objects with allocated storage duration, the lifetime begins when the allocation function returns (including the return from realloc) and ends when the realloc or deallocation function is called.
A pointer to an object (or one past the object) whose lifetime ended has indeterminate value.

Dangling pointers arise during object destruction, when an object that is pointed to by a given pointer is deleted or deallocated, without modifying the value of that said pointer, so that the pointer still points to the memory location of the deallocated memory.
If the program writes to memory referenced by a dangling pointer, a silent corruption of unrelated data may result, leading to subtle bugs that can be extremely difficult to find.

A common approach (glibc and bsd libc) is to copy bytes forwards from the beginning of the buffer if the destination starts before the source, and backwards from the end otherwise, with a fall back to the more efficient memcpy when there is no overlap at all.

In programming and information security, a buffer overflow or buffer overrun is a bug whereby a program writes data to a buffer beyond the buffer's allocated memory, overwriting adjacent memory locations.
Exploiting the behavior of a buffer overflow is a well-known security exploit.

For example, on a 32-bit machine, a data structure containing a 16-bit value followed by a 32-bit value could have 16 bits of padding between the 16-bit value and the 32-bit value to align the 32-bit value on a 32-bit boundary.

Effective type Every object has an effective type, which determines which lvalue accesses are valid and which violate the strict aliasing rules.

Strict aliasing Given an object with effective type T1, using an lvalue expression (typically, dereferencing a pointer) of a different type T2 is undefined behavior, unless: T2 and T1 are compatible types.

Although any pointer to object can be cast to pointer to object of a different type, dereferencing a pointer to the type different from the declared type of the object is almost always undefined behavior.

Object representation Except for bit-fields, objects are composed of contiguous sequences of one or more bytes, each consisting of CHAR_BIT bits, and can be copied with memcpy into an object of type unsigned char[n], where n is the size of the object.
Where strict aliasing prohibits examining the same memory as values of two different types, memcpy may be used to convert the values.
To avoid undefined behavior, the programmer must ensure that the aliasing assertions made by the restrict-qualified pointers are not violated.
In general, it is best to explicitly annotate all non-aliasing pointers in a function's prototype with restrict.

This is a common problem with functions that accept pointer arguments, and their tolerance (or the lack thereof) for aliasing must be carefully documented, particularly for functions that perform complex manipulations on memory areas passed to them.
As a result, aliasing makes it particularly difficult to understand, analyze and optimize programs.

Different threads of execution are always allowed to access (read and modify) different memory locations concurrently, with no interference and no synchronization requirements.

A program that has two conflicting evaluations has a data race unless either both conflicting evaluations are atomic operations one of the conflicting evaluations happens-before another (see memory_order) If a data race occurs, the behavior of the program is undefined.
Note that volatile variables are not suitable for communication between threads; they do not offer atomicity, synchronization, or memory ordering.

This means that within a single thread of execution, a volatile access cannot be optimized out or reordered relative to another visible side effect that is separated by a sequence point from the volatile access.

Objects of atomic types are the only objects that are free from data races; that is, they may be modified by two threads concurrently or modified by one and read by another.
Note that although each atomic object has its own modification order, there is no single total order; different threads may observe modifications to different atomic objects in different orders.
Built-in increment and decrement operators and compound assignment are read-modify-write atomic operations with total sequentially consistent ordering (as if using memory_order_seq_cst).
New code should always use the ‘__atomic’ builtins rather than the ‘__sync’ builtins.

The default behavior of all atomic operations in the language and the library provides for sequentially consistent ordering (see discussion below).
Typical use for relaxed memory ordering is incrementing counters, such as the reference counters , since this only requires atomicity, but not ordering or synchronization .
